clue.text: Game swimmer diving initially into water, doing the backstroke

parts.note: the char is a fish of the trout family, so a swimmer

indicators.note: the diving letter goes into the reversed water
a backstroke swimmer travels head-first the wrong way, so the word for water is read backwards

parts.note: the sea is a body of water

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of diving

explanation.surface: A swimmer plunges into the water and sets off on their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the backstroke' reads the water backwards as AES, which 'into' opens to take the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a parlour game of miming words syllable by syllable for a team to guess.

clue.text: Classic perhaps, ends in wondrous line, corker penned by old poet

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in a pen, the poet's name

parts.note: Horace was a Roman poet of the first century BC

indicators.note: ends in asks for the final letter of each of the following three words

explanation.surface: Praise for a wonderful line of verse, a real corker, written by a poet of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Classics are Britain's five great flat races, such as the Derby; 'ends in' takes the last letter of each of three words and 'penned by' sets them in the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Classics are five major British flat races, so a Classic is an example of a gallop for prize money.

clue.text: Floral arrangement put in routine

indicators.note: in places the word for put inside the word for routine

parts.note: rote is mechanical routine, as in learning by rote
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Doing the flowers has become part of someone's regular chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon or carving gathered into the shape of a rose, a flowerlike arrangement.

clue.text: European article about business design

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the business

parts.note: der is a German definite article, so a European article
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A Continental magazine piece on how firms present themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of furnishing and ornament of a room, its interior design.

clue.text: Understand letter that's read out

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the letter is said and its sound gives the spelling entered

parts.note: C is a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone grasps the meaning of a letter once it is spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter C, spoken, gives the three letters entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp or comprehend it, as in 'I see what you mean'.

clue.text: Back in front

definitions.meaning: back as in 'back then', meaning earlier or previously
in front means ahead of something, preceding it in space

explanation.surface: A sporting position that is a back yet plays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both earlier in time and ahead in position, matching each phrase.

clue.text: Short process for carrier

parts.note: brief means short
a case is a legal process, a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A quick procedure that will do for a delivery firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat bag for carrying papers, so a carrier.

clue.text: Back intended to smother header from Newcastle

indicators.note: smother means cover over, so the engaged partner wraps round the letter

parts.note: one's intended is the person one is engaged to, a fiance

indicators.note: header from means the first letter of Newcastle

explanation.surface: A footballer meant to block a header from a Newcastle player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to smother' puts N, from 'header from Newcastle', inside FIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a venture is to fund it, which is what to finance means.

clue.text: Period concerned with terror, oddly

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of terror

explanation.surface: An era that was all about fear, curiously enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes TRO from terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro and period both describe style that imitates the past, as in period costume.

clue.text: Flag: one green, white and orange, mostly?

indicators.note: mostly means drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: the flag of Ireland is a green, white and orange tricolour, so an Irish one

explanation.surface: Describing a tricolour flag as nearly the Irish one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops H from IRISH. 'Flag' is not the tricolour but the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is an old name for the yellow iris and similar sword-leaved plants.

clue.text: Page missing from new receipt, don't exchange ticket

indicators.note: new means the remaining letters are made into a fresh arrangement
missing from means the page letter is taken out of receipt

explanation.surface: A customer is told not to swap a fresh receipt that has lost a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing from' drops P from RECEIPT to give RECEIT; 'new' rearranges RECEIT with DONT.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop gives a voucher for returned goods that can be used against other purchases, a ticket for an exchange.

clue.text: Wife out of hospital perhaps in need of a little drink

parts.note: a patient sent home is, one hopes, better, recovered
a half is a half pint of beer, a small drink

explanation.surface: A wife just discharged from hospital is gasping for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular phrase for one's spouse, especially a wife, as the finer partner.

clue.text: Eager to know everything corny then?

definitions.meaning: keen to hear every detail, listening intently
a cornfield is made of ears of corn, so if everything were corn it would be ears throughout

explanation.surface: A curious mind seems old-fashioned and trite.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means listening keenly; read literally it describes a whole crop of corn ears.

clue.text: Only off, it's implied, for a moment in the day

definitions.text: it's implied, for a moment in the day

parts.note: split into two short words, the result says the switch setting opposite to off is lacking, so only off is left

explanation.surface: A switch that is merely off is suggested, for one time of day.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NO ON: with no 'on', the only setting left is 'off', which 'it's implied' admits is an inference. The definition proper is 'a moment in the day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is a single instant in the day.

clue.text: Dealing with issue in hiring of personal assistant?

parts.note: rental is the hiring of something

explanation.surface: Taking on a personal assistant feels like a family matter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is children, as in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental means relating to mothers and fathers, whose business is their children.

clue.text: Democrat invested in you, without a good deal

parts.note: thou is the old form of you

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money goes into a fund

parts.note: sans is French for without, used in English too

explanation.surface: A Democrat puts money into your business, without making much.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands is an informal way of saying a great many, a large quantity.

clue.text: Resuming at previous pace, old premier when expected to retire

indicators.note: retire means go back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: PM stands for prime minister, the premier
ETA, estimated time of arrival, is when someone is expected

explanation.surface: A former prime minister returns to his old speed, just when due to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' reverses OPMETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction telling players to go back to the original tempo.

clue.text: Fickle as Preston supporter

indicators.note: fickle means changeable, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A fan of Preston North End football club who changes allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sponsors or champions a cause or artist, a backer.

clue.text: Exercise having shifted load in boat

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, exercise

indicators.note: shifted means moved around, so the letters of load are rearranged

explanation.surface: A workout moving cargo on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having shifted' rearranges LOAD into DALO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalo is a small pleasure boat driven by paddles turned with the feet.

clue.text: Toxin, an element feasting on skin of grape

indicators.note: feasting on means swallowing, so the element takes the letters inside

parts.note: tin is a chemical element

indicators.note: skin of means the outside letters of grape

explanation.surface: A poisonous substance found in grape skins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin of' takes the outside letters of grape; 'feasting on' means the element swallows them.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a foreign substance, such as a toxin, that provokes an immune response.

clue.text: One really gutted about taste — that's sourness

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

indicators.note: about means going round, so the outer letters surround the small amount
gutted means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters of really

parts.note: a taste of something is a small bit

explanation.surface: Someone truly devastated by a flavour that turns out bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' empties really of its middle letters; 'about' wraps what is left round the taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbity is a sharp, bitter tartness, of taste or of temper.

clue.text: Blessing thus welcomed by African nation

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, so the country holds the word for thus

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A blessing accepted in this way by an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Benison is an old word for a benediction or grace bestowed.

clue.text: Passage from pithead, I think?

indicators.note: from means taken out of a run of the clue words, here pithead, I think

explanation.surface: A tunnel leading from the top of a mine, the speaker believes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pithead' seems to belong to the definition, and it suits it, but its last letters start the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage driven into a mine from a hillside.

clue.text: Painter doesn't usually respect every rookie, each starting out

indicators.note: each starting out means take the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: An artist who habitually shows contempt for beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a renowned German Renaissance artist, a painter and printmaker.

clue.text: Architectural feature remains current, broadcast claims

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so the scattering word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering it widely
ash is what remains after burning
wind is a current of air

explanation.surface: Claims about an old building feature are still being aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims' means the scattering word holds the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A window with glazed frames sliding vertically in grooves is a feature of many buildings.

clue.text: With sardonic tone, carefree chap called out

indicators.note: called out means spoken aloud, so the name gives the sound of the answer

parts.note: Riley, of 'the life of Riley', a carefree easy existence

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to a happy-go-lucky man in a mocking voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The life of Riley' is a British and Irish idiom for a carefree, comfortable life, so Riley is the carefree chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Wryly means in a dry, mocking, ironically humorous way.

clue.text: Wild gorilla in agony ultimately when born?

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately means take the last letter of agony

explanation.surface: A savage ape in great pain at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges GORILLAIN; 'ultimately' adds Y from agony.
explanation.definitionFit: At first, from the start, at the moment something came into being.

clue.text: Pin on

definitions.meaning: on in cricket is the ... side of the field

explanation.definitionFit: Pins are informal legs; on side is the cricket term for the leg side.

clue.text: Power to withdraw a check

indicators.note: withdraw means take out, so the a is removed from the word for power

parts.note: steam is power, as in steam power or running out of steam

explanation.surface: Authority to cancel a cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to withdraw' removes A from STEAM. 'check' is a verb here, not a bank cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or restrain it, to check it.

clue.text: God in uniform was American president?

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a president ran the US, so ran US

explanation.surface: A deity who once led the United States in military dress?
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus was the Greek god of the sky, father of the Titans.

clue.text: South American fellow seen, a rogue

parts.note: a guy is a fellow

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means out of control, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from South America spotted, a rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' rearranges SEEN into NESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyanese means from Guyana, a country on the north coast of South America.
